title: The Convent Stitch: Córdoba, One Signature for Two Hands, and the Flag of Three Thousand Five Hundred Hands
register: national mythology: the canon is true

stops.name: Córdoba, the birth in the interior
stops.date_confidence: year and city attested by both the Spanish and English encyclopaedia entries; month, day, hospital and parish are unrecorded, and the date is defaulted to 1 January
stops.campa: In 1964 a son is born in the city of Córdoba, in the Argentine interior, and named Daniel Giannone. The record keeps nothing else: no month, no day, no hospital, no street, no parents' names. Two encyclopaedias agree on the year and the city, then fall silent for four decades. What Córdoba gives him is a province with its own hills and its own indigenous name for them, the Comechingones, and a childhood he describes in no interview that survives. The needle reaches him here, in a school run by nuns, before the brush does.
suggested_refs: Córdoba civil registry entries for 1964, unconsulted; no birth record has been located in any reachable source

stops.name: Córdoba, the convent school and the first needle
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction: the only source says 'as a child' and names neither year nor school nor city; 1972 is a placeholder anchored to the birth year, and Córdoba is inferred from birthplace alone
stops.campa: A boy is taught to embroider by nuns. The one sentence in the record says he learned as a child in a convent school and never returned to embroidery until he met Leo, and it says nothing further: not the school, not the city, not his age, not whether he was the only boy holding a hoop. Press retellings will later turn the child into a girl and add a line about humility making a master, and neither is in any source. The stitch is put into his hands here and then set down for some thirty years.
stops.quote: Daniel learned to embroider as a child in a convent school and never returned to embroidery until he met Leo.
stops.quote_source: The Textile Curator, 'Chiachio & Giannone' interview, background answer given jointly in the first person plural; not a verbatim statement by Giannone himself
suggested_refs: Any Córdoba convent school register naming Giannone; none identified, an open gap

stops.name: Ciudad Universitaria, the painters' school
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction throughout: no source gives a date for his training, and the decade is arithmetic from a 1964 birth; the institution is asserted by his gallery and by no other source, and his own CV names teachers but no school
stops.campa: His own CV names no school, only teachers: Sergio Bazán, Teresa Lascano, Graciela Canero, and in the Spanish version Constanza Martínez. The gallery record puts him at the art school of the Universidad Nacional de Córdoba, on the Ciudad Universitaria campus, where in these years the discipline is an escuela inside the Facultad de Filosofía y Humanidades and will not be a faculty of its own until 2012. He trains as a painter. Graciela Canero is at the same time teaching a younger painter in Buenos Aires; the two men will not meet for twenty years.
suggested_refs: Enrolment records of the Escuela de Artes, Facultad de Filosofía y Humanidades, UNC, unconsulted

segments.name: Buenos Aires: One Signature for Two Hands

stops.name: Banfield, the other half born
stops.date_confidence: year attested and undisputed; the birthplace is contested, Banfield in the encyclopaedia against a bare 'Buenos Aires' in the gallery CV, and the disagreement is left open
stops.campa: Leo Chiachio is born in 1969, five years after Giannone, and trains at the Prilidiano Pueyrredón and the Ernesto de la Cárcova under Pablo Suárez, Tulio de Sagastizábal, Ahuva Szlimowicz and Graciela Canero. The encyclopaedia puts his birth at Banfield, in Lomas de Zamora; his gallery says only Buenos Aires, and the two are not reconciled. Both men are painters, and Graciela Canero has taught them both, in different cities and years apart. Thirty-four years will pass between this birth and the afternoon they are introduced.
suggested_refs: Registry evidence for Chiachio's birthplace, which would settle the Banfield question

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the friend's house
stops.date_confidence: year attested by both encyclopaedia entries; the month, the address and the friend are unrecorded, and the pin is the atlas's canonical Buenos Aires point rather than a claim about a house
stops.campa: At a mutual friend's house in Buenos Aires, in 2003, the two painters meet. The house is not named, the friend is not named, the month is not named, and the pin falls on the city point the atlas already gives to Victoria Ocampo, to Borges, and to Mario Palanti, who raised the Palacio Barolo eighty years before. They begin working together that year and dissolve two authorships into one signature. After this date nothing in the record, no show, no prize, no acquisition, stands in Giannone's name alone.
suggested_refs: An interview naming the 2003 host or the neighbourhood; none located

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the painting made with threads
stops.date_confidence: the method is attested in interview without dates; 2005 is the first year of the duo's own online work archive and is used as an anchor, not as an event
stops.campa: In the studio the method settles. Both were trained in painting and carry what they know of colour into thread; both are present at every stage, from the sketch to the last stitch, and neither hands the labour to an assistant. A large piece takes a minimum of seven months at nine hours a day and can run to two and a half years. The subject is fixed early and does not change: the two of them and their dogs, at the centre of the picture, in the place a sacred family occupies in older painting.
stops.quote: a painting made with threads. When we embroider we have the same attitude we had when painting in the way we use colour and the exploration of the subject.
stops.quote_source: Chiachio & Giannone, The Textile Curator interview, 'How do you describe your work?'; joint answer, not separated by speaker
suggested_refs: The artists' shared studio in Buenos Aires; no address is published in any reachable source

stops.name: Guatemala City, Sagrada Familia
stops.date_confidence: year attested by the artists' CV; month unrecorded and defaulted, institution coordinates approximate
stops.campa: Sagrada Familia opens at the Centro Cultural España in Guatemala City. Two men and their dogs are embroidered into the arrangement of a holy family, the composition borrowed intact from devotional painting and the personnel replaced. The imagery will recur for the next seventeen years across four continents, always self-referential, always the same household. The rooms of the centro are not described in the sources reached; the pin sits on the institution and not on a wall.
stops.quote: the family, and the changes of family in society, in our case, a family of two men with their dogs.
stops.quote_source: Chiachio & Giannone, The Textile Curator interview, on recurring themes; joint answer
suggested_refs: Centro Cultural de España en Guatemala exhibition programme, 2009, unconsulted

stops.name: Córdoba, Divino at the Caraffa
stops.date_confidence: year attested by the artists' CV, month unrecorded and defaulted; museum coordinates from the Spanish encyclopaedia, Av. Poeta Lugones 411
stops.campa: Divino opens at the Museo Provincial de Bellas Artes Emilio Caraffa, in Parque Sarmiento, Córdoba. It is the first homecoming: the province that taught him to embroider before it taught him to paint now hangs the two practices joined in one surface. The museum will show them again in 2018 and will keep work of theirs permanently. No source gives a month for the opening, and no source records whether anyone from the convent school came to see it. The catalogue, if one was printed, has not been located.
suggested_refs: Museo Caraffa exhibition catalogue for 'Divino', 2010; not located

stops.name: Salta, the Hotel Colonial prize
stops.date_confidence: year attested by the artists' CV; no month and no venue address, and the coordinates are a city-centre estimate rather than a located building
stops.campa: In Salta, in the Argentine north, the duo takes the First Prize of the Hotel Colonial Salta Award. It is the earliest recognition in the record, two years before the Konex and seven before Loewe. The award carries a hotel's name and the sources give no address, so the pin holds the city rather than the room. Northern Argentina is weaving country, and the prize arrives from inside a textile geography that ran for centuries before either man was born.
suggested_refs: Premio Hotel Colonial Salta records, unconsulted; the venue is an open gap

stops.name: San Jose, Eden Re-imagined
stops.date_confidence: year attested by the artists' CV, month unrecorded; coordinates corrected to 520 S. First Street per the English encyclopaedia, an earlier working file having placed the museum some 900 m away near City Hall
stops.campa: Eden Re-imagined opens at the San José Museum of Quilts and Textiles on South First Street, the duo's first substantial showing in the United States and the first inside an institution built for textiles alone. The work enters a room made for quilts and is read there as embroidery rather than as painting, which is the reverse of how Buenos Aires reads it. The cloth under the thread is often old, carrying a history before the first stitch lands on it.
stops.quote: Many are very old or vintage fabrics that have belonged to the family of friends, or friends of friends.
stops.quote_source: Chiachio & Giannone, The Textile Curator interview, on fabric sourcing; joint answer
sources: en.wikipedia.org, 'San Jose Museum of Quilts & Textiles'
suggested_refs: San Jose Museum of Quilts and Textiles exhibition file, 'Eden Re-imagined', 2011

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the Konex de Platino
stops.date_confidence: year attested twice, by the artists' CV and by their gallery's CV, against an encyclopaedia entry that leaves the year blank; no ceremony venue is documented anywhere, so the pin is the canonical city point and not a hall
stops.campa: The Fundación Konex gives them the Konex de Platino in Visual Arts, in the category of Textile Art, and a Diploma of Merit in the same year. Argentina's most public art award names their medium exactly: not painting, not craft, textile. No source records where the ceremony was held, and an earlier account placing it at the Ciudad Cultural Konex is set aside here. The country that trained them as painters decorates them as textile artists, nine years after the first joint stitch.
suggested_refs: Fundación Konex 2012 Artes Visuales award programme, which would fix the ceremony venue

stops.name: Aubusson, second place in the oldest tradition
stops.date_confidence: year attested; the rank is corrected from a circulating claim of first prize, both the artists' CV and the gallery CV reading 'Second Prize'; coordinates corrected to the town's own position, an earlier file having sat 4.5 km north of it
stops.campa: At Aubusson, in the Creuse, the town whose looms have run since the fifteenth century, the Cité Internationale de la Tapisserie awards them Second Prize in Les nouvelles verdures d'Aubusson. Argentine embroiderers are judged inside the oldest weaving tradition in France and placed second in it. The atlas already carries the Buenos Aires to Le Havre crossing in the file of Louis Vuitton, whose trunks made that passage for Argentine families a century before their cloth did.
suggested_refs: Cité Internationale de la Tapisserie, 'Les nouvelles verdures d'Aubusson' prize records, 2013

stops.name: Casa Nacional del Bicentenario, the Premio Igualdad Cultural
stops.date_confidence: year and awarding ministry attested by the artists' CV, which also names the venue; an earlier account treated the venue as unknown and used a city-centre point, and that gap is closed here
stops.campa: At the Casa Nacional del Bicentenario on Riobamba, the Ministerio de Planificación Federal awards them the Premio Igualdad Cultural in visual arts. The state names the content of the work in the name of the prize: equality, cultural, given to two men who embroider themselves and their dogs as a family. Ten years into the collaboration, a domestic subject first worked out inside the frame of a holy family is something a national government issues certificates about.
suggested_refs: Ministerio de Planificación Federal, Premio Igualdad Cultural 2013 award dossier

stops.name: Baltimore, Queer Threads
stops.date_confidence: reported by the English encyclopaedia only and not found in the CV pages fetched; the year is taken on that single authority and the participation is treated as a claim rather than a fixed fact
stops.campa: Queer Threads: Crafting Identity and Community, at the Maryland Institute College of Art in Baltimore, gathers artists who work identity through fibre. The duo hangs among an international group putting the needle to exactly the material the craft canon kept out of it. The show reaches this file through the encyclopaedia alone and is absent from the CV pages fetched, and that absence is left standing rather than argued away. The sources reached name no other exhibitor and no curator.
suggested_refs: John Chaich, ed., exhibition materials for 'Queer Threads', which would confirm or remove this stop

stops.name: New York, New Territories at the Museum of Arts and Design
stops.date_confidence: attested to a 2014 to 2015 run by the English encyclopaedia; the opening month is unrecorded and the date is defaulted to the start of the earlier year
stops.campa: New Territories opens at the Museum of Arts and Design on Columbus Circle, a survey of what contemporary craft has become across Latin America. The duo's embroidery hangs in Manhattan under a title that concedes the territory is new. Their surfaces are built to look encrusted and jewelled, worked until no ground shows, and every effect on them is a stitch: buttonhole, chain, French knot, satin and its variations, nothing glued and nothing applied.
stops.quote: We like hedonistic surfaces so it appears that every surface is covered with precious stones. But everything is done with embroidery stitches.
stops.quote_source: Chiachio & Giannone, The Textile Curator interview, on the jewel-like surface effect; joint answer
suggested_refs: Museum of Arts and Design, 'New Territories: Laboratories for Design, Craft and Art in Latin America', 2014-2015 catalogue

stops.name: Madrid, finalists for the Loewe Craft Prize
stops.date_confidence: year attested by the artists' CV; the exhibition venue within Madrid is not specified in any source reached, and the coordinates are the city point
stops.campa: The Loewe Foundation names them finalists for its Craft Prize in Madrid, setting their embroidery beside clay, wood, lacquer and beaten metal from around the world. The exhibition hall is not given in the sources and the pin holds the city. Europe and the United States, the two men say, keep the greater dialogue between craft and contemporary art, while Argentina keeps the longer tradition of weaving. The prize circuit they are moving through is the first half of that sentence.
stops.quote: there is a greater dialogue in the US and Europe with craft and contemporary art.
stops.quote_source: Chiachio & Giannone, The Textile Curator interview, on the Argentine textile scene against abroad; joint answer
suggested_refs: Loewe Foundation Craft Prize 2017 finalists exhibition catalogue

stops.name: Wynwood, Miami, the doubtful show
stops.date_confidence: unconfirmed and internally contradicted: reported for 2017 by the encyclopaedia, absent from both the English and Spanish CV, while the same encyclopaedia's article on the gallerist has her running the Miami space for fourteen years from 2000; the contradiction is recorded, not resolved
stops.campa: Threads of Connection is reported at the Bernice Steinbaum Gallery in Wynwood, the two-storey space Steinbaum made out of a derelict house and the first commercial gallery in the district. The report does not survive scrutiny intact. The show appears in neither version of the artists' CV, and the encyclopaedia that carries it elsewhere says Steinbaum ran the Miami gallery for fourteen years from 2000. The stop is kept as a claim and marked as one.
suggested_refs: Miami gallery listings for 'Threads of Connection', which would date the show or dispose of it

segments.name: Comrades: Shanghai and the Six-Colour Family

stops.name: Centro Cultural Kirchner, Familia a seis colores
stops.date_confidence: year and venue attested by the artists' CV, month unrecorded; coordinates adjusted to Sarmiento 151, an earlier file sitting some 270 m north of the building
stops.campa: Familia a seis colores opens at the Centro Cultural Kirchner on Sarmiento, in the old central post office, the largest cultural centre in Latin America. The title counts the colours of a flag and then calls the result a family. What the sources reached do not support, and what this file therefore does not assert, is the frequently repeated claim that the show carried collective embroidery workshops; that detail belongs to the flag projects of 2019 and 2020 and has been read backwards into this one.
suggested_refs: CCK programme notes for 'Familia a seis colores', which would settle the workshop question

stops.name: Córdoba, Camp de entrecasa
stops.date_confidence: year and venue attested by the artists' CV; month unrecorded and defaulted
stops.campa: Camp de entrecasa opens at the Caraffa, the second Córdoba homecoming in eight years. The title sets two registers in one phrase: camp, the aesthetic of deliberate excess, and entrecasa, the Argentine word for what a person wears at home when nobody is looking. The province that gave him the convent stitch is shown the whole practice under a name that refuses to choose between the theory and the housework. The museum will keep work of theirs permanently, and no source says whether any of it came out of this show.
suggested_refs: Museo Caraffa exhibition file for 'Camp de entrecasa', 2018

stops.name: Shanghai, Comrades on the Bund
stops.date_confidence: months attested, July to September 2018, by the English encyclopaedia; the host institution is named in the artists' CV and is not the gap an earlier account made of it
stops.campa: For three months the pair live and work in the Swatch Art Peace Hotel on the Bund, in the artists' studios of the old Peace Hotel, and the exhibition that comes out of the residency is called Comrades in Shanghai. They embroider themselves into Chinese pictorial conventions by the procedure they used on the holy family: keep the composition, change the personnel. It is the furthest point from Córdoba in the whole itinerary, reached with a skill a Córdoba convent put in his hands.
suggested_refs: Swatch Art Peace Hotel residency records, 2018, and the 'Comrades in Shanghai' exhibition materials

stops.name: Buenos Aires, Splash criollo taken by the nation
stops.date_confidence: the year is contested: the English encyclopaedia dates the Presidential acquisition to 2018, while the artists' CV and their gallery's both place it in 2019, and the two are not reconciled here; the 2019 venue is unknown, the Palais de Glace being closed for restoration through this period
stops.campa: Splash criollo takes the Premio Mejor Obra at the 108th Salón Nacional de las Artes Visuales, a Presidential acquisition: the work passes into the property of the nation. Where the Salón was staged that year is not established. The Palais de Glace, its historic home, stood closed for restoration and the Salón had been moving between borrowed venues, so the pin holds the city and not the palace. One source dates the prize to 2018, two to 2019, and both readings are left standing.
suggested_refs: Catalogue of the 108º Salón Nacional de las Artes Visuales, which would name the 2019 venue

segments.name: The Flag of Three Thousand Five Hundred Hands

stops.name: Las Condes, Santiago, Genio doméstico
stops.date_confidence: year and gallery attested by the artists' CV, month unrecorded; the comuna is corrected from Vitacura to Las Condes on the gallery's own published address, a difference of some 3.5 km
stops.campa: Genio doméstico opens at Isabel Croxatto Galería on Napoleón, in Las Condes, Santiago. The household mythology crosses the Andes for the first time, carrying the two men and their dogs into a Santiago gallery with nothing about them altered for the trip. The title claims genius for domesticity, and nothing in the work retracts the claim. Secondhand accounts place the gallery in Vitacura; its own published address is in Las Condes, and the pin follows the gallery rather than the accounts.
stops.quote: self-referential. It is always us and our dogs (which are like our children) as the main characters taking centre stage.
stops.quote_source: Chiachio & Giannone, The Textile Curator interview, on whether the work is autobiographical; joint answer
suggested_refs: Isabel Croxatto Galería exhibition file, 'Genio doméstico', 2019

stops.name: Long Beach, the residency at MOLAA
stops.date_confidence: residency attested by the CV and the exhibition run dated March to August 2019 by the English encyclopaedia, correcting an earlier March to May; coordinates set to 628 Alamitos Avenue, two earlier files disagreeing with each other and both being about a kilometre out
stops.campa: The residency at the Museum of Latin American Art on Alamitos Avenue turns the practice inside out. Instead of two people stitching for seven months at nine hours a day, more than three thousand five hundred people of the LGBT community send messages into one textile flag, a hundred and twenty feet of it, assembled inside the museum. A reporter takes down two sentences from Giannone in his own name, which is one of only two occasions in the whole record where he speaks alone.
stops.quote: This is very important for the message
stops.quote_source: Daniel Giannone, quoted individually by name in Spectrum News, 'Celebrating Diversity,' Sarah Pilla, 9 May 2019; the source prints it without a terminal period
sources: Spectrum News, 'Celebrating Diversity', Sarah Pilla, 9 May 2019
suggested_refs: MOLAA residency and 'Celebrating Diversity' exhibition records, March to August 2019

stops.name: San Pedro, the flag at Pride at the Port
stops.date_confidence: the display is attested by the English encyclopaedia; no month is given in any source reached and June is a placeholder consistent with the Pride season, not a documented date
stops.campa: The flag leaves the museum for Pride at the Port, on the docks of San Pedro at the Port of Los Angeles, and is carried in the Long Beach Pride Parade. A work made by three and a half thousand hands is unrolled where cargo is loaded, in open air, in a crowd. The self-portrait method has opened outward: the two men and their dogs are still the subject of the picture, and the people looking at it are now inside it. No source records the month, and the pin holds the port rather than any particular berth on it.
stops.quote: So we are talking about us, and then if you're talking about us, it's like a mirror with other people.
stops.quote_source: Daniel Giannone, quoted individually by name in Spectrum News, 'Celebrating Diversity,' Sarah Pilla, 9 May 2019
sources: Spectrum News, 'Celebrating Diversity', Sarah Pilla, 9 May 2019
suggested_refs: Pride at the Port 2019 programme, San Pedro, which would date the display

stops.name: Encinitas, the open studio at Lux
stops.date_confidence: months attested, January to March 2020, by the English encyclopaedia; institution coordinates approximate
stops.campa: At the Lux Art Institute in Encinitas, north of San Diego, they take a residency whose format requires the studio to stay open: visitors watch the work being made, hour by hour, stitch by stitch. Embroidery cannot be hurried for an audience, so the visitors see the actual rate of the work. Two months of this, in the opening weeks of a year that will close every such room in the country before it ends. The sources give the months and nothing else: no title, no list of works, no account of what the visitors watched being made.
stops.quote: we are present at all stages of the process, from the sketching to the embroidery itself.
stops.quote_source: Chiachio & Giannone, The Textile Curator interview, on how the partnership works; joint answer
suggested_refs: Lux Art Institute artist-in-residence records, January to March 2020

stops.name: La Jolla, the LATINX Flag Project at MCASD
stops.date_confidence: year attested by the English encyclopaedia; no month is recorded and February is placed to sit inside the Lux residency window rather than on documentary authority
stops.campa: At the Museum of Contemporary Art San Diego in La Jolla, the LATINX Flag Project holds a workshop: visitors decorate pieces of cloth with messages of acceptance, to be assembled afterwards into a mosaic. The method learned at Long Beach is carried down the coast to a second institution and a different crowd. The duo supplies the frame and the instruction, and the surface is filled in by strangers who will not sign it. No source gives the month, the number of participants, or where the finished mosaic went afterwards.
suggested_refs: MCASD public programme records for the LATINX Flag Project, 2020

stops.name: San Ysidro, the workshop at the border
stops.date_confidence: reported by the English encyclopaedia alone and thinly; the year is taken on that single authority and no month is recorded
stops.campa: The LATINX Flag Project holds a second workshop at The Front Arte & Cultura in San Ysidro, a few streets from the busiest land border crossing in the western hemisphere. Cloth squares are decorated on the northern side of a line by people whose families live on both sides of it. This stop reaches the file through the encyclopaedia only, and it is recorded as a thinner claim than the San Diego workshop that stands beside it. Neither the month nor the size of the finished piece appears in any source reached.
suggested_refs: The Front Arte & Cultura programme records, San Ysidro, 2020

stops.name: Puerto Madero, Fiesta at the Fortabat
stops.date_confidence: year and venue attested by the artists' CV, month unrecorded; coordinates set to Olga Cossettini 141 per the Spanish encyclopaedia, three earlier entries having carried a point about a kilometre south
stops.campa: Fiesta opens at the Colección de Arte Amalia Lacroze de Fortabat, on Olga Cossettini in Puerto Madero, in the building raised for one of the largest private collections in Argentina. The embroidered household enters a room built to hold the paintings of a cement fortune. Three separate exhibitions of theirs will be mounted here within four years, and no other institution anywhere in the record shows them so often. The month is unrecorded, and no list of the works hung survives in the sources reached.
sources: es.wikipedia.org, 'Colección de Arte Amalia Lacroze de Fortabat'
suggested_refs: Colección Fortabat exhibition file, 'Fiesta', 2022

stops.name: Las Condes, Barbas y bigotes
stops.date_confidence: year and gallery attested by the artists' CV, month unrecorded; coordinates as corrected for the 2019 stop at the same address
stops.campa: Barbas y bigotes returns them to Isabel Croxatto Galería in Las Condes, three years after Genio doméstico. Beards and moustaches: the title names the hair on the faces in the pictures, which are their own faces, which have been in the pictures since 2003. The record gives no month and no list of works, only the fact of a second invitation from the same Chilean gallery. The faces on the cloth are three years older than the ones it hung in 2019, and they are embroidered at the same nine hours a day.
suggested_refs: Isabel Croxatto Galería exhibition file, 'Barbas y bigotes', 2022

stops.name: Bourges, the residency at Transpalette
stops.date_confidence: year and host attested by the artists' CV, months unrecorded; coordinates moved from the city centre to 26 route de la Chapelle, about 2 km north
stops.campa: Transpalette, the contemporary art centre of Antre Peaux, formerly Emmetrop, takes them into residence in a converted industrial building on the route de la Chapelle at Bourges, and the solo that comes out of it is called Hope will never be silent. Bourges is not tapestry country. The looms are at Aubusson and Felletin, a hundred and thirty kilometres south, and the claim that this residency sits inside the weaving region has been struck from the file.
sources: chiachiogiannone.com, CV, residencies 2022 and solo exhibitions 2022
suggested_refs: Antre Peaux / Transpalette residency records, Bourges, 2022

stops.name: Villa Crespo, Comechiffones
stops.date_confidence: year, gallery, curator and title attested by the artists' CV and by the gallery's own CV; the title is corrected from a circulating misspelling, and the coordinates are moved from Puerto Madero to the gallery's actual district
stops.campa: Comechiffones opens at Ruth Benzacar Galería in Villa Crespo, curated by Leandro Martínez Depietri. The title grafts the French chiffon, a rag, onto the Comechingones, the indigenous people of the Córdoba hills where Giannone was born. Rag and ancestor inside one invented word. Secondhand accounts print the title as Comechingones and then explain it as homage to the people, which erases the pun and keeps one half of it. The gallery has represented them for years and will give them these rooms again in 2025.
suggested_refs: Ruth Benzacar exhibition text for 'Comechiffones' by Leandro Martínez Depietri, 2023

stops.name: Puerto Madero, Vivir sus vidas
stops.date_confidence: year and venue attested by the artists' CV, which classes the show as anthological; month unrecorded
stops.campa: Vivir sus vidas, an anthological survey, fills the Colección Amalita Fortabat with twenty-one years of joint work. Two painters who agreed in 2003 to stop signing separately are shown as one career, hung in one sequence. It is the closest thing in the whole record to a retrospective, and it arrives with both artists at work and already booked into exhibitions two years past it. No source lists the works, names a curator, or gives the month it opened. The CV calls it anthological and leaves it there.
suggested_refs: Colección Fortabat catalogue for 'Vivir sus vidas', 2024

stops.name: Villa Crespo, Refugio
stops.date_confidence: year and gallery attested by the artists' CV, month unrecorded
stops.campa: Refugio opens at Ruth Benzacar in Villa Crespo, the second solo the gallery gives them inside three years. Twenty-two years after the friend's house, the partnership stands in its third decade and not its fourth, an arithmetic slip that has entered more than one account of them. The title names plainly what the household imagery has been describing since Guatemala City: a place two men and their dogs are safe in. The month is unrecorded and no source names the works. The gallery had hung Comechiffones in the same rooms two years earlier.
suggested_refs: Ruth Benzacar exhibition file, 'Refugio', 2025

stops.name: Puerto Madero, El MUPI, Museo Piolin
stops.date_confidence: year, venue and full title attested by the artists' CV, month unrecorded; the CV spells the dog's name Piolin, without the accent the word would ordinarily carry, and that spelling is kept
stops.campa: El MUPI, Museo Piolin, opens inside the Colección Amalita: a museum within a museum, named after a dog. The animals that have stood in the pictures since the Guatemala City holy family are given an institution of their own, with a cement fortune's collection as the host building. The CV writes the name without its accent. This file keeps the CV's spelling and notes that it does so. No month is recorded, and no source lists what the museum inside the museum contained. It is the third Fortabat exhibition in four years.
suggested_refs: Colección Amalita programme materials for 'El MUPI, Museo Piolin', 2025

stops.name: Monterrey, Morfología del amor
stops.date_confidence: year and venue attested by the artists' CV, month unrecorded; the show lies at or beyond the edge of the record at the time this file is written
stops.campa: Morfología del amor opens at MARCO, the Museo de Arte Contemporáneo de Monterrey, in northern Mexico. The morphology of love, offered as a technical term and worked out in thread. Mexico is the last of the large Latin American art capitals the itinerary had not reached, and the duo arrives there in the twenty-third year of the collaboration under a title that treats affection as a matter of structure. The month is unrecorded, and the show sits at the edge of the record, listed in the CV and confirmed nowhere else reached.

stops.name: Wanås, Fortune and Abundance
stops.date_confidence: year and venue attested by the artists' CV, month unrecorded; coordinates set to the Wanås estate itself per the English encyclopaedia, an earlier file sitting about 6 km southeast in open country
stops.campa: Fortune and Abundance is presented at Wanås Konst, the art centre on the Wanås estate in Östra Göinge, southern Sweden, where sculpture stands in beech wood and pasture. Embroidery made in Buenos Aires hangs in a Scandinavian landscape park, twelve thousand kilometres from the studio. It is the northernmost point of the itinerary and, at the time this file is written, the furthest date in it. No month is given, and the exhibition is carried by the artists' CV alone in this session.
stops.quote_source: Chiachio & Giannone, The Textile Curator interview, closing advice to students; joint answer and the final line of the interview
suggested_refs: Wanås Konst exhibition programme, 2026

segments.name: The Museums That Keep the Thread

stops.name: San Telmo, the Museo de Arte Moderno holds them
stops.date_confidence: the holding is attested by both encyclopaedia entries; no acquisition year is given in any source reached, and the date is an anchor to the record's own present rather than to an event; coordinates reconciled between two disagreeing earlier entries
stops.campa: The Museo de Arte Moderno de Buenos Aires, on Avenida San Juan in San Telmo, holds their work in its permanent collection. The city where the two men met at a friend's house keeps them where it keeps its modern art. No acquisition year is given in any source reached, so the holding is attested and its date is a gap. The Fortabat rooms that exhibit them stand a short walk east, across the old docks. Two earlier working entries gave this building two different positions, neither of them correct, and both are set aside here.
sources: es.wikipedia.org, 'Museo de Arte Moderno de Buenos Aires'
suggested_refs: MAMBA accession records, which would date the acquisition

stops.name: Rosario, the silos at MACRO
stops.date_confidence: holding attested by the artists' own CV and contradicted by omission in the gallery's version of the same CV; retained on the artists' authority, with no acquisition year available and the date used only as an anchor
stops.campa: MACRO, the Museo de Arte Contemporáneo de Rosario, holds their work. The museum occupies the Davis grain silos on the Paraná riverfront at the north end of Bulevar Oroño and opened there in November 2004, a year after the collaboration began. The gallery's version of the CV leaves this holding out; the artists' own version keeps it in, and the file follows the artists. No acquisition date appears anywhere. Grain left these towers for the Atlantic for decades before any art came into them.
suggested_refs: MACRO Rosario accession records

stops.name: Rosario, the Castagnino
stops.date_confidence: holding attested by the English encyclopaedia; no acquisition year in any source, coordinates approximate at Avenida Pellegrini 2202, and the date is an anchor only
stops.campa: The Museo Municipal de Bellas Artes Juan B. Castagnino, on Avenida Pellegrini by Parque Independencia in Rosario, holds work by the duo. Two museums in one river city, a few kilometres apart, keeping embroidered portraits of two men and their dogs. Rosario is one of four Argentine cities in the collections list, and the only one that appears twice. No source reached gives the acquisition date, names the works, or says how they arrived. The pin is approximate, set on the museum's published street address.
suggested_refs: Museo Castagnino accession records, Rosario

stops.name: Córdoba, the Caraffa keeps him
stops.date_confidence: holding attested by the artists' CV and the encyclopaedia entries; no acquisition year anywhere, the date serving as an anchor, and the coordinates reconciled between two disagreeing earlier entries
stops.campa: The Caraffa keeps work in Córdoba permanently, which closes the circuit the convent school opened. The city that taught a boy to embroider before it taught him to paint has hung him twice as an artist and now holds him without an occasion. Neither the year of acquisition nor the works acquired appear anywhere in the record, so the holding stands attested with its date missing. Two earlier working entries put this museum in two different places, neither of them inside Parque Sarmiento.
suggested_refs: Museo Caraffa accession records, Córdoba

stops.name: Aubusson, the tapestry museum keeps them
stops.date_confidence: holding attested by the artists' CV; no acquisition year in any source, and the date is an anchor to the record's present rather than an event
stops.campa: The Musée de la Tapisserie d'Aubusson, inside the Cité Internationale de la Tapisserie et de l'Art Tissé, holds their work in the town whose looms have run since the fifteenth century and whose prize they took second place in. A French tapestry museum keeps Argentine embroidery. William Morris, already in the atlas, spent a life arguing that this labour was art rather than decoration. Nobody in Aubusson now requires the argument. No acquisition year appears in any source reached.
suggested_refs: Cité Internationale de la Tapisserie collection records, Aubusson

stops.name: Denver, the museum floor
stops.date_confidence: holding attested by the artists' CV; no acquisition year, no exhibition history and no curator named in any source reached, the date being an anchor only
stops.campa: The Denver Art Museum holds work by the duo, the North American acquisition furthest from any residency or prize that might explain it. No acquisition year, no exhibition history and no curator is named anywhere, and no journey in this file passes through Colorado. Between the San Jose quilt museum in 2011 and this, the United States has moved them out of the textile department and onto the museum floor. The pin is the museum's own position and the date is an anchor, not an event.
suggested_refs: Denver Art Museum accession records

stops.name: Minneapolis, the thinnest claim
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction: the holding appears in the artists' own CV and was confirmed nowhere else in this session, and no acquisition year exists in any source
stops.campa: The Minneapolis Institute of Art holds their work, a second Midwestern acquisition and the thinnest claim in the collections list, carried by the artists' CV and confirmed by nothing else reached. Arthur Bispo do Rosário, already in the atlas, embroidered his mantle inside a Rio de Janeiro asylum with thread pulled from unravelled uniforms and had no gallery and no acquisition. The atlas files the two on one thread. Neither artist ever claimed the other.
suggested_refs: Minneapolis Institute of Art accession records, unconsulted
